title: N-Queens II

statement.hi:
`n x n` chessboard pe `n` queens aise rakhni hain ki koi do queens ek dusre ko attack na karein (same row, column ya diagonal nahi).

Is version me **row 0 ki queen column `col` (0-indexed) pe fixed hai**. Aise kitne distinct arrangements possible hain, wo count return karo. (Saare `col` ka sum original N-Queens II ka answer hai.)
statement.en:
Place `n` queens on an `n x n` chessboard so that no two queens attack each other (no shared row, column or diagonal).

In this version **the queen in row 0 is fixed at column `col` (0-indexed)**. Return the number of distinct arrangements. (Summing over every `col` gives the original N-Queens II answer.)

hi: Har row me exactly ek queen hogi, to row-by-row queen rakho.
Used columns, `row - c` diagonals aur `row + c` anti-diagonals ko sets/arrays me track karo taaki check O(1) ho.
en: Every row holds exactly one queen, so place queens row by row.
Track used columns, `row - c` diagonals and `row + c` anti-diagonals in sets/arrays so each check is O(1).

explain.hi: n = 4 ke 2 solutions hain; unme se ek me row 0 ki queen column 1 pe hai.
explain.en: n = 4 has 2 solutions; in one of them the row-0 queen is in column 1.

explain.hi: Corner pe queen rakhne se n = 4 ka koi solution nahi banta.
explain.en: With the queen in a corner, n = 4 has no solution.

approach.hi:
Row 0 me queen ko `col` pe rakho aur uska column + dono diagonals mark karo. Phir row 1 se backtracking: har row me har safe column try karo, recurse, undo. Row `n` tak pahunche to 1 count karo.
Teen boolean arrays (`cols`, `row - c + n`, `row + c`) se safe check O(1). Time ≈ O(n!).
approach.en:
Put the row-0 queen at `col` and mark its column and both diagonals. Then backtrack from row 1: in each row try every safe column, recurse, undo. Reaching row `n` counts as 1.
Three boolean arrays (`cols`, `row - c + n`, `row + c`) make the safety check O(1). Time ≈ O(n!).
